headline: Word Grouping Puzzle Game for ESL Vocabulary Classes
outcomes: Students identify hidden semantic categories linking groups of four words, building vocabulary depth
Develop critical thinking by testing and rejecting possible groupings before committing
Encounter topic-relevant vocabulary in a puzzle context that rewards careful analysis over quick guessing
Build pattern recognition skills transferable to reading comprehension and exam tasks
howItWorks: The AI generates 16 words on your chosen topic, secretly grouped into four categories of four
Students see the 16 words on their device and attempt to identify and select one complete group
Correct groups are revealed with the category name; incorrect attempts cost points
The round ends when all four groups are found — or when the timer expires
teacherUseCases: Vocabulary review at the end of a unit — students must categorize rather than just recall
Topic introduction that surfaces prior knowledge before teaching new vocabulary
Critical thinking challenge where the difficulty lies in the deceptive 'trap' group

faq.q: How does the puzzle difficulty work?
faq.a: The AI generates four groups with increasing subtlety: one easy group (obvious category), two medium groups (overlapping vocabulary), and one hard 'trap' group where words seem to belong elsewhere. The difficulty setting increases how deceptive the groupings are.

faq.q: Can the class work together on the puzzle?
faq.a: Yes. In whole-class mode, the puzzle is displayed on the board and students discuss groupings collaboratively. In individual mode, each student works on their own device and the class compares results.

faq.q: What if the AI creates a category that doesn't make sense?
faq.a: Teachers can review the groups before starting and reject a round. The AI regenerates fresh content on demand, so finding a replacement takes seconds.

faq.q: How do students interact with the 16-word grid?
faq.a: Each student needs a phone or tablet with a browser. They tap words to form groups on their own device. No download, app, or student account required — they join via the session link.

faq.q: Is this suitable for exam prep?
faq.a: Yes. The deductive reasoning and vocabulary precision required in Connections maps well to vocabulary sections in Cambridge and IELTS exams.
